'''Johanna Barbara Stachel''' (born 3 December 1954 in [[Munich]]) is a German [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]]. She is a professor in experimental physics at the University of Heidelberg ([[Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg]]). Stachel is a former president of the [[German Physical Society]] (DPG).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Johanna Stachel – Munzinger Biographie|url=https://www.munzinger.de/search/go/document.jsp?id=00000025276|website=www.munzinger.de|access-date=9 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Johanna Stachel ist Einsteins Erbin|url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/wissen/erste-frau-an-der-spitze-der-physiker-johanna-stachel-ist-einsteins-erbin/6511846.html|newspaper=Der Tagesspiegel Online|language=de|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Johanna Stachel|url=https://www.physi.uni-heidelberg.de/~fschney/stachel.html|website=www.physi.uni-heidelberg.de|access-date=8 May 2020}}</ref> 

==Early life and education==
Johanna Stachel completed secondary education in 1972 at the Spohn Gymnasium in [[Ravensburg]]. She studied physics and chemistry at [[Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz]] and the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]] (ETH Zürich) and received a degree from the [[Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz]] in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr.Johanna Stachel|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Stachel_Johanna_D.pdf|website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref> In 1982 she obtained a doctorate in physics from the same university.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Stachel|first=Johanna|url=https://hds.hebis.de/ubmz/Record/HEB073730262|title=Die neutronenreichen Rutheniumisotope, ein Übergangsgebiet zwischen sphärischen und asymmetrisch deformierten Kernen|publisher=Mainz Univ., Dissertation|year=1982|location=Mainz|trans-title=Neutron-rich ruthenium isotope, a transition domain between spherically and asymmetrically deformed nuclei}}</ref><ref name="bio">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/about/governance/election/stachel.cfm|title=Johanna Stachel|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=11 October 2018|archive-date=11 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181011214625/https://www.aps.org/about/governance/election/stachel.cfm|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

==Career==
From 1983 to 1996, Stachel studied and worked at the [[State University of New York]] (SUNY) at [[Stony Brook, New York|Stony Brook]] and [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] where she met her future husband professor [[Peter Braun-Munzinger]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Stern-Gerlach-Medaille 2019 – Interview: Prof. Dr. Johanna Stachel and Prof. Dr. Peter Braun-Munzinger|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C9FgLfWoX9k|last=Deutsche Physikalische Gesellschaft|date=6 May 2019|website=YouTube|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref> In 1996 she was named professor at the [[Heidelberg University|University of Heidelberg]]. Stachel was spokesperson of the [[Super Proton Synchrotron|CERN SPS]] experiment [[NA45 experiment|CERES/NA45]] and directed the developed the [[ALICE experiment#Transition radiation detector|ALICE Transition Radiation Detector.]]<ref name=bio/>

Stachel was elected [[German Physical Society#Presidents|President of the German Physical Society]] for a two-year term starting in 2012. Her two primary priorities as president were first to defend basic research by showing its importance and promote physics education in schools by improving the training of physics teachers and the standards across German schools.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tagesspiegel.de/wissen/erste-frau-an-der-spitze-der-physiker-johanna-stachel-ist-einsteins-erbin/6511846.html|title=Johanna Stachel ist Einsteins Erbin|last=Schubert|first=Frank|date=16 April 2012|work=Der Tagesspiegel Online|access-date=7 October 2018|language=de-DE|issn=1865-2263}}</ref>

During her career, she has delivered over 150 lectures at international workshops and conferences and has participated in over 100 seminars and colloquia.

==Research interests==
Stachel's research focuses on understanding [[relativistic heavy-ion collisions]] and [[Quark–gluon plasma|quark-gluon plasma]]. She is member of the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] [[ALICE experiment|ALICE Collaboration]] at [[CERN]] in Geneva. Stachel is also interested in developing detectors that are needed to carry out these experiments in particle physics.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scitecheuropa.eu/alice-experiment-large-hadron-collider/88807/|title=Professor Johanna Stachel discusses the effort of German physicists in the ALICE experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider|date=3 September 2018|work=SciTech Europa|access-date=7 October 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Johanna Stachel discusses the effort of German physicists in the ALICE experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider|url=https://www.scitecheuropa.eu/alice-experiment-large-hadron-collider/88807/|last=Garner|first=Courtney|date=3 September 2018|website=SciTech Europa|language=en-GB|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref>

==Offices and honorary offices==
Among her academic responsibilities are:

* From 2003 to 2005 she was dean of the faculty of Physics and Astronomy of the University of Heidelberg.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fak. f. Physik und Astronomie: Dekan, Prodekan etc.|url=http://www.physik.uni-heidelberg.de/dekane.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031008154557/http://www.physik.uni-heidelberg.de/dekane.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 October 2003|date=8 October 2003|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref> Until 2012, she continued to serve as vice-dean.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Telefonverzeichnis|url=http://univis.uni-heidelberg.de/form?dsc=go&to=tel&department=130000|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060814213452/http://univis.uni-heidelberg.de/form?dsc=go&to=tel&department=130000|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 August 2006|date=14 August 2006|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=13 June 2012|title=Universitätsrat|url=https://backend-484.uni-heidelberg.de/sites/default/files/documents/2018-10/jahresbericht_2011.pdf|journal=Jahresbericht|language=de|volume=2011|pages=16}}</ref>
* Associate editor for the journal [[Nuclear Physics A]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/nuclear-physics-a/editorial-board|title=Nuclear Physics A Editorial Board|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160728173531/https://www.journals.elsevier.com/nuclear-physics-a/editorial-board|archive-date=28 July 2016}}</ref>
* Membership of the Advisory Board of the Wilhelm and Else Heraeus Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stiftungsorgane: Wilhelm und Else Heraeus-Stiftung|url=https://www.we-heraeus-stiftung.de/stiftung/stiftungsorgane/|website=www.we-heraeus-stiftung.de|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190317232311/https://www.we-heraeus-stiftung.de/stiftung/stiftungsorgane/|archive-date=17 March 2019|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref>
* Membership of the University Council of the Vienna University of Technology starting in 2018 for a 5-year term.<ref>{{Cite web|title=University council|url=https://www.tuwien.at/en/tu-wien/organisation/university-management/university-council/|date=26 February 2020|website=www.tuwien.at|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200216050637/https://www.tuwien.at/en/tu-wien/organisation/university-management/university-council/members/|archive-date=16 February 2020|access-date=11 May 2020}}</ref>
* International councilor with the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name="bio" /> from 2016–2019.

On 28 March 2014 she received the [[:de:Kategorie:Ehrenmitglied_des_Physikalischen_Vereins|honorary membership of the ''Physikalischen Verein'', Frankfurt]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Deiss|first=Bruno|date=7 April 2014|title=Neues Ehrenmitglied des Physikalischen Vereins|url=https://www.unireport.info/50256125/unireport-ausgabe-2-14.pdf|journal=UniReport|language=de|volume=47|issue=2|pages=10}}</ref> where she is listed along with [[Heinrich Hertz]], [[Albert Einstein]] and [[Otto Stern]].
